messages:
josh: Heads up — after the NAT gateway route tweak last night a subset of ap-south GPU nodes failed to fetch ephemeral keystore tokens during bootstrap. Seeing ~12/120 unable to join the warm pool. Logs show repeated decrypt timeouts. :unamused:
priya: ugh. which route change? I rolled a narrower CIDR to close a leak — surprised it affects the keystore proxy. :eyes:
alex: getting these in the keystore proxy logs: `ERROR decrypt: kms.DecryptTimeout: 10s exceeded` and `upstream connection reset` right after the route change window. Could be that privatelink traffic now egresses via the NAT and hits a proxy with stale routes.
rachel: from a security/audit perspective we lost full keystore access events for ~40m during the window — sampler shows spikes in retry counts. We should preserve the request ids for compliance. Can we surface them to the audit shipper?
sam: SRE side: nodes that failed to join are stuck in Booting -> WaitingForKeystore. Warm pool capacity dropped ~10% so prod burst headroom was reduced but no user impact yet. Rewarm is in progress but slow because decrypts failing early.
josh: attaching a snippet of the bootstrap failures: ```
[2026-03-20T01:12:43Z] boot: fetch-keystore failed id=inst-azb-07 err="kms.DecryptTimeout"
[2026-03-20T01:12:44Z] boot: retry 1/5
[2026-03-20T01:12:47Z] boot: fetch-keystore failed id=inst-azb-07 err="upstream connection reset"
```
priya: trying a quick revert of the route table  — will post when done. If that's it we need a safer rollout (canary route + smoke).
ops-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: keystore-decrypt-timeout spike in ap-south at 2026-03-20T01:10:00Z — 87 events in 5m. Pager duty: engaged.
deploy-bot: Canary rollback executed for route-table rtb-08aef; change id: chg-20260320-rtb. Rolling back to previous route CIDR.
alex: after rollback I still see some TLS handshakes failing from NAT IPs to privatelink endpoints. Might be conntrack/stateful NAT exhaustion on the new NAT gateway. Quick check: `ss -s` on the proxy showed conntrack > 600k.
lina: cost note — we briefly hit the regional NAT burst limit which pushed some egress onto a fallback transit gateway; that increased egress metered charges for ~30m. We should estimate incremental cost for billing.
rachel: we need the audit logs for the failed decrypt attempts. Priya, can you keep the rollback id and exact timestamps? Security requires request ids and affected instance ids for the audit timeline.
priya: logged: chg-20260320-rtb rollback at 2026-03-20T01:16:12Z. I captured the route table diff and exported to S3: s3://infra-debug/ap-south/2026-03-20/rtb-diff.txt
sam: immediate mitigation: 1) scale proxy pod replicas + bump conntrack timeout 2) queue warm-pool rewarm with backoff 3) mark instances that failed for manual re-provision if rewarm fails. I'm already scaling proxy x3.
josh: longer-term: we should make keystore traffic prefer privatelink and fail closed to NAT, and add canary gating for any egress routing changes that touch keystore/privatelink prefixes. Also add preflight that validates conntrack headroom.
alex: added a temporary iptables rule on the proxy host to reject new connections from NAT IPs that look like stale sessions — reduced retry noise. snippet: ```sudo iptables -I INPUT -s 100.64.12.0/24 -j DROP``` (we'll roll this back once the NAT is rebalanced)
lina: I'll run a cost estimate and add the spike to the monthly anomaly tracker. Probably a few hundred dollars in egress + NATGW burst fees; tagging it under incident-2026-03-20-keystore-route.
rachel: security follow-ups: 1) preserve decrypt request ids in longterm audit bucket 2) add alert for keystore samplers > threshold 3) postmortem entry required for compliance.
priya: rewarm is slowly recovering — warm pool at 95% now. I left the rollback in place and will schedule a controlled redo of the route change with canary prefixes next week.
sam: adding actions to oncall runbook: - preflight script to verify privatelink reachability: `curl --resolve keystore.internal:443:10.0.1.5 https://keystore.internal/health` - conntrack check snippet - a cost estimate step if NAT burst fallback is used.
josh: great. final action items: (1) eng-infra (priya/alex) to build canary rollout + preflight (2) eng-sre (sam) to update runbook + conntrack automation (3) eng-platform (josh/lina) to add cost alert and audit preservation (4) eng-security (rachel) to draft compliance note. We'll reconvene after the controlled redo. :thumbsup:
